rationale.usefulness: The repository-aware controller offers a concrete trial for recurring coding, teaching-repository, website and code-based video work. The report explains what to inspect, preserve and measure rather than advertising the research percentages as a plugin discount. The mismatch between paper stopping and plugin alerts is particularly useful.
rationale.impact: Cross-session black-box cost control has meaningful potential in coding-agent workflows, supported by multiple host/model settings and task domains. Limited benchmark continuity, historical model choices and different shipped defaults keep the evidence short of broad operational validation. Impact 6 maps to 1,800–2,200 words; the frozen body has 1,949, subject to the final mean.
rationale.novelty: The coordinated use of operational micro-skills, tool pruning and failure-loop intervention is a meaningful experience-driven approach. The report does not suggest model retraining or wholly new primitives, and observed gains depend on recurring environment structure.
rationale.maturity: Documented host ranges, settings, recovery mechanisms and a runnable plugin support bounded use. Experimental adapters, notification gaps, micro-skills disabled by default, the non-stopping plugin and absent independent native trials materially limit production confidence. Benchmark quality regressions are explicitly retained.
rationale.openness: MIT source, an accessible paper and separate experiment harness/task sets provide strong methodological inspection and reproducibility opportunities. Paid or provider-controlled agents and moving main-branch compatibility constrain portability and exact repetition, so openness is strong but not complete.
